condition: critically ill adults in the intensive care unit
title: RapidMeta Critical Care | Conservative vs liberal oxygen therapy in the ICU
hero_h2: Conservative vs liberal oxygen targets in critically ill adults
nyt_headline: How Much Oxygen in Intensive Care?

pico.pop: Critically ill adults in the ICU (mechanically ventilated or with acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure)
pico.int: Conservative / lower oxygenation target (PaO2 ~55-90 mmHg or SpO2 ~88-96%)
pico.out: All-cause mortality at the longest follow-up each trial reports (HOT-ICU 90d, ICU-ROX 180d, LOCO2 28d, Oxygen-ICU ICU-stay)
pico.subgroup: ARDS (LOCO2) vs general ICU vs acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure

trials.name: HOT-ICU
trials.group: Lower (PaO2 60 mmHg) vs higher (90 mmHg) oxygenation; acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure

trials.name: LOCO2
trials.group: Conservative (PaO2 55-70) vs liberal (90-105) oxygen in ARDS; stopped early

trials.name: Oxygen-ICU
trials.group: Conservative (PaO2 70-100) vs conventional oxygen; single-centre, stopped early

trials.name: ICU-ROX
trials.group: Conservative vs usual oxygen; mechanically ventilated. ANZCTR-registered (no NCT); 180-day mortality reported as an odds ratio, pooled by generic inverse-variance
